Subject: Delayed responses from Redwood for several endpoints

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing a sustained increase in response times across our inference calls to the hosted endpoint (model: rwd/med-13b). Symptoms started ~07:40 PST and p99s for generation are in the 9–12s range (normally ~1.4s). Affected routes are /v1/generate and /v1/stream for our production token. This is directly impacting patient-facing flows.

Sample request ids: 8f7a2a1d, 8f7a3c4e, 8f7a4f99. Attached a short trace and a few payload examples. Can you confirm if you have an incident on your side? Please escalate — we need an ETA or a mitigation we can implement client-side.

Thanks,

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and the traces, that's helpful. We've opened an incident (RY-20261101-auroramed) and published an initial advisory on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RY-20261101-auroramed.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Triage: Ops has been paged and is investigating autoscaling and queuing for the hosted pool handling your token.
- Temporary mitigation: routing rule created to move your production token to a non-shared, higher-priority pool to reduce queueing. This should begin applying within ~5–10 minutes.
- Data collection: we requested full traces and request logs from your attachments; our team will correlate with internal request ids.

Can you confirm whether you are able to temporarily reduce batch sizes or switch streaming to non-chunked responses as a quick client-side mitigation? We don't want to disrupt your flow but that can reduce pressure while we complete the routing change.

I'll keep you updated as we have concrete progress. Looping in Marissa (incident lead) and Sean (platform reliability) for technical follow-up.

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 8:12 AM Alicia Barnes <alicia@auroramed.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sustained increase in response times across our inference calls...

Hi Alicia, Karthik — quick ops update from the incident team:

What we observed:
- From ~07:35–08:20 PST a subset of requests routed to the public hosted pool experienced queueing due to an autoscaler race on the GPU-backed tier. The autoscaler repeatedly scaled up but there was a lag in instance readiness combined with an unexpected KV-cache invalidation flood (rare) which increased per-request overhead.

Mitigations applied (completed at ~10:35 PST):
- Forced routing switch for AuroraMed token to the dedicated high-priority pool; ongoing connections are being drained from the shared pool.
- Enabled model-variant fallback: requests that would have hit the 13b fp16 path are temporarily served by a quantized 13b variant with equivalent semantics but faster startup.
- Short-term KV-cache grace window extended to reduce invalidation amplification.

Impact and next steps:
- We saw measurable p99 improvement beginning ~10:40 PST; downstream effects normalized by 10:55 PST for the majority of traffic. We're still monitoring for tail latency anomalies and will keep the routing in place for 24–48 hours while we complete a root cause analysis.

Attachments: auroramed_incident_timeline.pdf (timeline + initial traces).

If you can share any additional request ids that hit after 10:45, please send them and we'll cross-check.

—Marissa Cole
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia, Carlos — following up with a final customer-facing update.

Summary:
- Incident RY-20261101-auroramed impacted a portion of your production traffic between ~07:35 and ~10:55 PST on Nov 1; p99s increased due to an autoscaler readiness lag amplified by an unusual KV-cache invalidation pattern.
- We applied routing and model-variant fallbacks; observable client impact returned to baseline by ~10:55 PST.

What we will deliver:
1) A concise written postmortem (root cause, timeline, and corrective actions) by EOD Nov 4.
2) A 60-minute follow-up call (ops + engineering) next week to walk through the postmortem and answer questions. Please let me know your preferred day/times; we can coordinate.
3) As a goodwill gesture for the disruption to patient flows, we'll apply a 10% credit to your November usage invoice; our finance team will confirm next steps.

Immediate ask: if you still see any elevated latency for requests after Nov 2 18:00 PST, reply with request ids and we'll re-open the bridge immediately.

Thanks again for the quick customer-side diagnostics — the traces helped us correlate the events faster. We're treating the KV-cache invalidation pattern as the top priority for engineering remediation to avoid recurrence.

Best,
